repair:bounces.notes_for_integrator:
Behaviour changes others will notice:
1. A spam complaint is now kept per account and address (table mail_complaints). Two triggers in db.ts put recipients.complained_at back whenever an address that complained turns up on that account's envelopes, including new ones and corrections. The old trigger recipients_address_changed is dropped and recreated in migrate. Undoing a complaint now needs a 6-digit code emailed to the recipient; POST /sign/:token/mail-again answers code_sent first, then changed. Undoing withdraws the mail provider's report (abuse_reports.status 'withdrawn', a new value; the operator queue only lists 'open').
2. emails.bounce_reason now holds only our plain words. The mail server's text is in the new column emails.bounce_said, shown only in the dev outbox. The evidence export (evidence.ts) reads bounce_reason and so now carries plain words only.
3. Address-only provider news is applied only when one sender wrote to that address in 3 days. A provider id that matches nothing is never matched by address.
4. A hard bounce of an email that has about_user set (an invitation, a team notice) no longer marks the login.
5. POST /envelopes/:id/correct may answer {ok, not_emailed:'marked_as_spam'}, and writes a 'Not emailed' line to the record.
6. mail.ts tooLate() drops a queued email to a complained recipient, and a queued request or reminder to a bounced one.
7. forgetEnvelopes (routes-trust.ts) calls rememberGoneMail before deleting an envelope's emails while the account stays.
8. /mail/events can answer 202 with a note after 8 seconds; more than 5000 events gets 413.

Promises in copy (all shown only when MAIL_EVENTS_TOKEN is set):
- help #bounced: the email at once depends on the 'When something needs you' setting; a person can undo by mistake on the signing page.
- COMPLAINT_MEANS: account-wide, survives correction, try again and new envelope, undone with a code.
- The processing page: who sees the raw reason, mail_gone kept 30 days as a fingerprint, mail_complaints kept until undone or the account is deleted.
New copy says 'Sign&Grow' where the brand appears, for the rename pass.

For the owner to confirm:
- Complaints apply to the whole account (all team members), which is how I read 'a new envelope' in your decision.
- Withdrawing the report on undo.
- The 3 codes a day.

repair:tplroles.notes_for_integrator:
Behaviour changes others will notice:
1. A copy of a template that is not for everyone, or is locked, made by someone who may not set its rules (only its owner, an admin or the account owner may), now belongs to the template's owner. This covers /clone, POST /envelopes {kind:'template', template_id} and Save as template. Before, only locked copies made by non-changers did. The /clone answer's 'locked' is now the real value, not always true. A 'Copied' history line names who made the copy.
2. On an envelope from a locked template, an API caller that sends 'recipients' without 'note' or 'access_code' (which empties them) gets 403 wording_locked when the template gave that person a note or code. The editor always sends both.
3. POST /envelopes/:id/correct can no longer take off a code check or access code the locked template gave.
4. Cloning an envelope from before its template was locked is refused (403 wording_locked) for whoever the lock is for.
5. GET /files/:id/content answers 404 for a document of a template the caller may not use, unless an envelope or template they can open holds the same file.
6. The shared .sn-choice input rule gets flex-shrink: 0.
7. CheckFields has an optional keepCode prop; nothing changes unless it is passed.
Decisions for the owner to confirm:
(a) The subject of a locked envelope stays open, as the builder left it; it is now said plainly everywhere. An altered subject is emailed.
(b) A template saved from an envelope by a member who may not set the rules lands under the owner's name with that member's edits. The history line says who; the list does not.
(c) A member can still clone their own envelope as an envelope after its template became admins-only. They already hold the document; only the lock case is refused.
Seen, out of scope:
- GET /files/:id/content still serves any other member's envelope file by id inside the account. Envelopes are private to their sender, but files are account-wide. This existed before; the template case is now closed.
- probe2 K: a comment 'for everyone' pinned on a locked envelope can contradict the locked wording.
- The lifecycle invite-address clash the builder noted is unrelated.
abuse_and_stuck: Abuse, handled and tested: copy a restricted HR template and open it to the team, by /clone, by POST kind template, by Save as template, by browser or key. The copy stays Maya's; widening and unlocking are refused; Chad and Otto still cannot reach it.

Abuse, handled and tested: a chosen changer copies a locked template to lift the lock or publish it unlocked. The copy is Maya's and locked; he cannot set its rules or delete it. He can still publish it as a form, as he can the original.

Abuse, handled and tested: on a locked envelope, replace the template's 'Note for you', drop the code check or access code, or turn the signer into a signing group, by PUT or by /correct after sending. Each is refused 403, nothing is saved, and the email keeps the template's note.
Abuse, handled and tested: keep minting unlocked envelopes by cloning a draft from before the lock. Refused with words; the template is the way.
Abuse, handled and tested: read the HR PDF by its file id after the template became admins-only. 404, the same as a missing file.
Abuse, handled and tested: repeat a bulk call with its Idempotency-Key after losing the template. The rows left are not sent and say why.

Abuse, left open: the subject of a locked envelope can be changed to something misleading (owner decision); a comment for everyone can sit beside the locked wording; any member can still upload their own altered PDF (help says so).
Abuse, left open: Save as template from a freely edited envelope of an unlocked restricted template puts that member's edits under the owner's name. The history line names the member.
Stuck, handled: Otto wants his own version of a restricted template. The page offers Use, not 'Make my own copy', and says a copy would be Maya's and to ask her (screen 02). Refusals say the same.
Stuck, handled: Otto's old draft cannot be cloned after the lock. The toast says why and to use the template (screen 05).
Stuck, handled: Otto needs to remove the code check for someone. The editor does not offer 'none' and says the check comes from the template and who to ask (screen 03); the admin and Maya can.
Stuck, handled and tested: Maya deleted her own locked template. She can still change her envelopes and save one as a template; others are told to ask her or an admin.
Stuck, handled and tested: Maya's or the admin's bulk send fills a prefilled column on a locked template and goes out.
Stuck, handled and tested: a chosen member leaves. The template history says so, with who did it, so Maya sees why the rule sentence changed.

- The provider callback has a new error code, signed_in, added to SIGNIN_ERRORS. A browser with a session no longer gets a new login from Google or Microsoft unless it carries an invitation. An expired or replaced state for a signed-in browser goes to /app/settings?tab=profile&signin_error=expired instead of /login.

- POST /public/check/dispute and POST /sign/:token/dispute now accept a code or link from retired_tokens, so any email we ever sent the person works.

Behaviour changes others will notice:

(7) The view token format changed (it is bound to the address and browser). A page left open across the deploy gets 'Load the page again and press the button there.' once.

(9) DELETE /clickwraps/:id answers 409 'reported' while a report is open.

repair:logic.notes_for_integrator:
Behaviour changes others will notice:
- Every field from GET /envelopes/:id and GET /sign now carries calc_num, which is set only for calculated fields.
- GET /sign also returns 'inputs' (a key or null) and 'formula_inputs' (array). The 'others' entries for a finished person's calculated field carry 'num'.
- POST /sign/:token/complete accepts 'inputs'. It can now answer 409 code 'changed' with why 'inputs'. A caller that sends no key is held to the key it was last given (recipients.seen_inputs); a person who never loaded GET /sign after this change is not held to anything.
- New 400 refusals on save: code 'logic_chain' (more than 100 fields in one line), and a number of more than 15 digits written in a formula. A formula saved earlier with such a long literal can no longer be read, and is shown as 'cannot be read'.
- A save or Finish that chooses two radio buttons of one group is refused. Choosing one now clears the others of the group on the server.
- applyValues has an optional 5th parameter and returns the hidden set. hiddenAfter no longer exists.
- Two new columns: fields.calc_num and recipients.seen_inputs.

Decision for the owner to confirm: Calc.value is now exactly the number shown. A formula that uses another calculated field therefore counts the shown number: {t}=1/3 shows 0.3333333333, and {t}*3 gives 0.9999999999, not 1. I chose this so a total worked out on the spot and one read back from storage always agree, and anyone checking the printed numbers by hand gets the same result. The other choice is to keep full precision in calc_num.

Legal and copy: no legal claims were added. All new screen text is plain, and new copy says Sign&Grow only where it already did.

Probes in tests/out/verify-logic that now behave differently by design:
- probe1 stops at the long literal, which is now refused. The copy at tests/out/repair-logic/probe1-after.ts runs to the end.
- probe7 stops because sending the stacked 1.000/1000 fields is now refused.
- probe2 and probe3 still call liveLogic with v.others instead of formula_inputs. probe2 is correct now anyway, because others carry num. probe3 shows 'another field' instead of an id. The page itself uses formula_inputs.

Fragile test, for others: my PDF tests count every image on page 1 (2 and 1). If another engineer starts drawing an image on page 1, such as a QR code, those counts need updating.

Seen but out of scope: lifecycle.test.ts:1260 fails against the public-forms page source.

repair:groups.found:
The builder's signing groups were in place and tests/groups.test.ts had 26 tests, all passing. I ran the skeptic's probes (tests/out/verify-groups/probe1-5.ts) before changing anything, and every finding reproduced exactly as written. Output is saved in scratchpad/probes-before.txt.

- Spam marks (probe1 A and C). A member's complaint was kept for the account, but notifyMembers never read it. Ben got "Reminder: Staff handbook" after marking spam. The remind answer said reminded 1 and did not name him. His page had mail_stopped false, and mail-again was refused (409, not in MAY). After Maya marked spam and handed it back, she was reminded again as a member.
- Bounce (B). The sender was told to "choose Correct next to Maya Lopez". Doing that answered 400.
- Hand-back note (F). The PayPal lure text reached Ben's "Back with HR team" email.
- Sender in the group (D). Signing for the group used 1 signature; signing directly used 0.
- Group swapped after signing (E). The new group's row stayed free=1, so the total used stayed 1.
- Removed member (probe2 G). The check page answered genuine, status sent, with her url.
- Template whose group was deleted (J). Each bulk row failed, 2 drafts were left behind, and the message said "Open the envelope".
- Template use naming a person for the group's role (K). Accepted and quietly ignored.
- Send-scope key (L). GET /groups answered may_change true.
- Access code (O). Ben, whose colleague had it, froze the group's code (423 for Maya too). His 2 asks for the code used up hers (429).
- Certificate (N). It said "Viewed | Ben Ortiz, for HR team".
- Member added by a correction (probe3 1, probe4 1). When the same save moved a field, Dee's only email was "Updated". When a colleague had it, Dee got nothing, while the editor and openapi promised an email.
- Give back while paused (probe4 3). The route answered {ok:true}, nobody was emailed, and the toast said "Every member was emailed their link."
- Hand-back limit (probe4 4). Ben's first hand-back got 429 because Maya had used the group's 3.

The report lists no regressions. The screens list has no problems.

A report on a member's link or with a member's security code (POST /sign/:token/report, /public/check/report) sets the member's mark and answers mail_stopped:true; the report dialog then tells them. complaint() in routes-bounces.ts now names the member and the group ('Ben Ortiz <...>, a member of HR team ... The other members are not affected ... Only Ben Ortiz can undo that'). When the person who had taken it on is the one who complained, the email adds that they still get nothing after a hand-back. 'mail-again' is now in MAY (open/copy/taken). Each member gets their own code (new table member_mail_again, and the code's hash includes the member id), so one member's code never undoes another member's mark. done.item: 1. Provider from settings, no temperature, low reasoning, retry once without it on a 4xx, about 1200 tokens, streamed, built-in answers when down, slow (55 s) or empty
done.how: src/lib/chatprovider.ts picks the provider, first match wins: SUPPORT_CHAT_API_KEY (+ SUPPORT_CHAT_BASE_URL, default OpenRouter, + SUPPORT_CHAT_MODEL, default moonshotai/kimi-k3-20260715), then MOONSHOT_API_KEY (api.moonshot.ai, kimi-k3), then OPENROUTER_API_KEY. A base URL must be https; plain http is allowed only for localhost. The function returns the name of the key's setting, never the key. src/server/chat.ts sends stream:true and max_tokens 1200, with no temperature. It asks for low reasoning in each host's own spelling and tries once more without it after a 4xx. The answer is relayed to the page as SSE events (open/think/d/done). The built-in answers (src/server/chatkb.ts) take over with no key, when the host can't be reached or answers 5xx, after CHAT_TIMING 55 s, or when the answer is empty or the stream errors. The page is told which. An answer cut short by the timeout keeps its text and is marked cut. Closing the page aborts the call to the model.

done.item: 6. Limits in SQLite: 8/minute and 60/day per address, per signing link, per account, daily total SUPPORT_CHAT_DAILY_LIMIT (2000); past any, built-in answers and told plainly
done.how: chat_counts table (db.ts SCHEMA) keyed by HMAC fingerprint and slot (minute/day). admit() checks and counts all buckets in one transaction: address (an IPv6 address counts as its /64) 8/min and 60/day, link 40/day, account 300/day, everyone SUPPORT_CHAT_DAILY_LIMIT (0 means none go to the model). Past any limit: the built-in answer plus limitText() naming the limit and the time it frees up (local time in the dialog). The daily-total limit is logged once a day. Only questions sent to the model are counted. An in-memory flood guard refuses more than 60 a minute from one address in plain words. API keys, other sites (Origin) and non-JSON posts are refused.
done.test: tests/chat.test.ts: 'one internet address gets 8 questions a minute...' (incl. IPv6 /64, no raw IP in DB), 'and 60 a day; a signing link 40 a day; an account 300 a day; everyone together...' (incl. unknown link counts nothing, 0 sends nothing, built-in answers not counted), 'a flood is refused in plain words; a key, another site and a form post are refused'.
done.left_open: These are limits on cost, so they can be used against others. Many addresses can use up the daily total, and then everyone gets the built-in answers until midnight UTC. One team member can use up the account's 300. Whoever holds a signing link can use up its 40. A person is still one click away in every case. With TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0, every visitor shares one address count, as with the app's other limits.

build:stamp.notes:
The user-facing text says "Sign&Grow" throughout, as asked. Nothing was renamed.

Other sessions were editing the same files while I worked: envelopes.ts, routes-sign.ts, pdf.ts, the sign page, routes-trust.ts, cron.ts and tsconfig. After every change notice I re-checked that my hooks were still in place. Their in-progress edits broke the build twice for a few minutes (linkProvider, then hiddenAfter); both times I waited and reran.

Their work-in-progress commits have also picked up some of my files. I ran no git command that changes anything.

Design choices to know about:
- Stamp pictures are stored in the database (stamp_images, keyed by the SHA-256 of the PNG), not as blob files. They are pruned when nothing points at them: from removeUnusedBlobs, after a stamp is deleted, and by the timer. Unlike blob files, they are therefore not covered by FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (same as signature images).
- A stamp field's value is the picture's SHA-256. The sender's own stamp keeps its picture from the moment it is first saved, in drafts and templates too. The editor offers "Use it as it is now" when the team's stamp has changed since.
- I found and fixed one bug in review: Duplicate and Copy to every page in the editor would have been refused for the sender's stamp. A copy now keeps its twin's picture. It is covered in the tests.

Browser check: tests/out/build-stamp/look.cjs, with screenshots in tests/out/build-stamp/. I looked at the Settings dialog and list, the editor inspector, the maker on desktop and phone, the phone page before and after, and the text view. The dev server is stopped, .next-build-stamp and its temporary data folder are deleted, and the sample generator is in my scratchpad (make_samples.py).

One limit: a black-ink stamp printed on top of black text cannot be separated by colour. The "Cut off the edges" control is the way out for such a photo.

per_sample.sample: 1 round seal (clean design, blue)
per_sample.looks_like: A clean vector seal tinted a light cornflower blue (solid ink renders about rgb 73,95,175) and laid over the page with multiply. The placement is right: the black rule and 'Company stamp' show through, there is no box, and it is a believable 38 mm across. The ink itself, though, is one flat translucent tint with perfect circles and font-perfect letters.
per_sample.what_gives_it_away: The density is the same everywhere. In the stored PNG, ink alpha p10 to p90 is 0.81 to 0.91, and after the 0.9 opacity no pixel ever reaches full ink, so the whole stamp looks like a graphic with its opacity turned down. Edges are vector-perfect with only anti-alias softness. Letters have no darker rim. You cannot see the heavier side. The specks are sub-pixel at real size: a radius of about 1 to 3 px in a 906 px image shown at about 150 px. The blue is too light and too 'screen' for stamp-pad ink.

per_sample.sample: 2 RECEIVED box (clean design, red)
per_sample.looks_like: A stock 'RECEIVED' clip-art stamp in salmon-pink red (rgb about 208,77,86), tilted about 3 degrees, multiplied over the page so 'Company stamp' reads through 'DATE:'. The tilt and the double frame help, but the colour is perfectly even and every stroke edge is crisp.
per_sample.what_gives_it_away: Flat, uniform pink tint with no ink-starved areas, no dark stroke rims and no visible voids. The frame lines are perfectly straight and even in width. Real red stamp ink is a duller, darker carmine, not rose-salmon.

per_sample.sample: 3 Chinese name seal (clean design, red)
per_sample.looks_like: A square seal in the same rose-pink, slightly tilted, text showing through. In the signed PDF the ink is almost a single flat colour: the lightness std over the solid ink is 2.0 out of 255.
per_sample.what_gives_it_away: A real seal-paste impression is deep vermilion and heavily mottled, often with broken frame corners and grainy fill. This one is even, pinkish and clean-edged, so it reads as a digital overlay. The thick frame is the place where uneven pressure would show most, and it shows none.

per_sample.sample: 4 photo of a round seal (purple)
per_sample.looks_like: The most convincing of the six. Some of the photo's own unevenness survives, so the stroke weight and edges wobble a little and the ink is slightly mottled. It sits on the page well, tilted, with the text showing through.
per_sample.what_gives_it_away: The colour is a light lavender (about 124,82,164) and too pale for violet stamp ink. There are still no voids or skips you can see at real size, no darker stroke rims and no pressure gradient. Recolouring to one flat RGB also removes the small hue shifts a real impression has.

per_sample.looks_like: A blue seal with some real texture carried over from the photo. It is close to an impression at real size, but at 200 percent you can see parallel pale bands crossing the outer ring at regular spacing, plus small spurs on the inner ring, where the ruled lines of the paper were.

per_sample.what_gives_it_away: It does not read as a stamp at all. The large solid disc sits at about 55 percent density (rgb about 221,125,132) with a few white pin-dots, the punched-out leaf has razor edges, and the brand name is missing. It looks like a pink sticker.

changes: Make the texture work in millimetres at the printed size, not in pixels of the 1000 px stored image. Today, in src/lib/stampink.ts rubber(), the specks have a radius of about 1 to 3 px and the fine grain has cells of about side/260 px. Both disappear when a 40 mm seal is shown at about 150 px on screen and at about 470 px at 300 dpi. Target sizes: voids 0.15 to 0.6 mm across, about 20 to 60 per seal; paper-grain modulation at 0.1 to 0.3 mm over the whole body of the ink, not only where v < 0.92; and two or three ink-starved patches of 3 to 8 mm where density falls to 35 to 60 percent.

Turn texture into local variation instead of a global fade. Today the default ink alpha sits between 0.81 and 0.91 (p10 to p90), max texture only lowers it to 0.69 to 0.82, and texture 0 actually gives the most ink-like colour. Let the core of the strokes reach full ink (alpha 1.0) and make the unevenness come from patches, grain and voids. Then raise STAMP_OPACITY in src/lib/stamps.ts to 1.0 (or at least 0.97): multiply alone already lets the printed text show through.

Make the heavier side visible. The current lean term changes density by about 5 percent at the default setting. A real hand-pressed stamp often goes from full ink on one side to 50 to 65 percent on the other, sometimes with a short arc of the outer ring almost missing. Use a gradient of roughly 0.35 to 0.5, plus an occasional faint arc segment chosen from the seed.

Add ink squeeze at stroke edges. Darken a band 0.08 to 0.2 mm wide along every stroke edge, by 10 to 20 percent, and let the middle of wide solids (the star, a thick ring, a filled disc) run 10 to 25 percent lighter, so the darker rim reads the way it does on a real impression. Compute it from a distance-to-edge map or from the plane minus a blurred copy. Today rubber() makes edges lighter, the opposite of real ink.

Replace the blur softening with rough, slightly spread edges. Today soften() is a 3x3 blur that only reads as anti-aliasing. Instead, threshold the ink plane against a noise field (v' = smooth(0.5 - 0.15 + n*0.3, ..., v)) so the edge moves by 0.03 to 0.1 mm, then dilate by about 0.05 mm of dot gain, so lines are a touch bolder and not vector-perfect.

Use duller, darker stamp-pad colours and let solid areas reach them. Today solid ink renders about rgb 73,95,175 (cornflower), 208,77,86 (salmon pink) and 124,82,164 (lavender). Aim for blue-violet about 40,45,125 (hue 235 to 245), carmine red about 170,30,48, violet about 80,40,120, and blue-black about 35,36,48.
Vary the colour a little within the impression: dense areas slightly darker and more saturated, thin or starved areas a bit lighter and cooler. One RGB with only alpha changing is a digital tell.

Logo input (sample 6): when findInk reports several colours, do not keep a pale large solid and punch holes where other colours were. Base the ink strength on darkness against the paper for all marks, or tell the user plainly that a multi-colour logo will not make a believable stamp. Also stop orange from counting as 'red' (inkOfHue sends hue 45 to 75 to red). The current default output, a pale pink disc with a leaf-shaped hole and the name gone, should not be offered as an impression.

Photos on ruled paper (sample 5): before extracting the ink, detect and remove long thin straight lines that run across the whole photo, or fill them in where they cross the ink. The ruled lines currently leave evenly spaced pale bands across the outer ring and small spurs on the inner ring.

Re-check at the sizes people actually see: render each sample at 40 mm on a 96 dpi screen (about 150 px) and in the PDF at 150 and 300 dpi, and require that voids, the darker rims and the pressure gradient can still be seen there, not only in the 1000 px stored file.

changes: Never delete the wording of a design by default. When findInk reports several colours on a clean design (not a photo), default onlyInk to false and print every mark in the chosen ink. Keep 'only the X marks' as an opt-in for photos with foreign print around the stamp. Do not let a fill colour (the orange disc, hue 32) become the 'ink' that decides what survives: weight text-like thin marks above large fills, and treat orange (about 15 to 50 degrees) as its own class, not red. Today sample 6 loses the company name GreenCo by default.

Map strength to ink like rubber: anything that is clearly a mark prints at full ink density, and only antialiased edges stay partial. A steep curve after strengthOf (for example smooth(lo, lo+0.12) instead of a 0.3 ramp) turns tinted logo fills (orange disc at alpha 0.63) into solid ink, so they stop printing as pink halftone. For logos, offer to knock out inner shapes of another colour (leaf, vein) so they stay visible inside a solid area.

Faint or worn photographed stamps lose their smallest text. Test: /tmp/judge-1-1/in-faint-photo.jpg, a lightly inked seal where 'Reg. No. LSK/2019/04417' and 'P.O. BOX 40217-00100 NAIROBI' are clearly readable. Output at the default settings (/tmp/judge-1-1/w-faint-photo-t0.5-236x3.png) drops both lines and the C of COMMISSIONER, and 'Keep faint marks' does not recover them (/tmp/judge-1-1/w-faint-p0-236x3.png). Causes: the fixed paper cut (lo 0.21), a faint-boost driven by the 96th percentile of the whole stamp (the heavy ring dominates), onlyInk's saturation gate smooth(0.06,0.16,s) (faint ink has low saturation against its paper), and rubber() thinning edges below 0.92. Fix: set the cut from the stamp's own histogram (for example Otsu on ink distance inside the stamp's box), normalise strength locally over a window of about 3 to 5 mm (capped), and apply onlyInk's hue test only where saturation is above noise, keeping low-saturation pixels next to accepted ink.

Make the ink darker and real-coloured. The strongest ink on the page is only about 78 percent coverage (alpha median 0.85 to 0.88, max 0.94 to 0.98, then opacity 0.9). Measured darkest-5-percent colours: blue (68,91,172), red (208,76,85), purple (119,76,161), which read as periwinkle, coral pink and lavender. Let the cores of strokes reach alpha 1.0, keep 0.9 to 0.95 opacity only for paper show-through, and pick INK_RGB values that land on stamp-pad colours after multiply: violet-blue about (45,50,135), dull red about (170,35,45), purple about (85,40,120).

Size the texture in millimetres of the printed stamp, not in pixels of the 1000 px store, so it survives the 4x to 7x downscale to 150 to 450 px on screen and 236 px at 150 dpi. Voids 0.2 to 0.6 mm, mottling 2 to 6 mm, edge jitter 0.05 to 0.15 mm. Today the 1 to 2 px specks and the side/260 grain average away, and even 'a well-worn stamp' (texture 1) looks flat at real size (/tmp/judge-1-1/w-dense-seal-t1-236x3.png). Keep the readability guard by limiting voids per stroke: thin rings of 0.12 mm and 1 mm type survived every setting I tried, so there is room.

Widen and shape the density variation the way a pressed stamp varies: about 0.55 to 1.0 across the impression, a clear heavier side from the pressure lean (now only 10 percent), slightly darker rims on letters (ink squeezed to the rubber's edges) instead of the current lighter, softened edges, and solid areas mottled with paper showing through in patches. Replace the 3x3 blur with edge displacement plus a little ink gain, so edges are rough rather than vector-smooth with a blur.

Apply the tilt as a transform on the page (CSS rotate on .st-print, and pdf-lib rotate with the matching offset) instead of baking it into the pixels. Otherwise a rectangular stamp is shrunk to fit its turned box inside the unturned field: the RECEIVED stamp prints about 8 to 10 percent smaller than the 52 x 26 mm the sender set.

Move or blur the blue/purple boundary at 250 degrees. Common blue-violet stamp ink sits at 245 to 255 degrees, so a one-colour photo straddles it. My faint violet-blue photo came back several=true, share 0.64, which shows the 'more than one colour, like a logo' notice for a plain stamp. Treat hues within about 25 degrees of the main hue as the same ink.

Keep the parts that already work: multiply plus no box (printed text and lines show through on screen and in the PDF, and the two match), true 38 to 40 mm size on the page, stored resolution (330 to 577 ppi in the PDF), seeded tilt, paper and ruled-line removal on photos, and readable thin rings, small ring text and CJK strokes at real size. All tests and outputs are in /tmp/judge-1-1/ (run.mts runs the project's own stampink.ts; the w-*.png and c-*.png files are real-size composites).

changes: Fix paper detection for coloured paper in src/lib/stampink.ts paperOf. The 'greyish' gate (saturation under 0.3) rejects kraft (about 0.45) and canary-yellow copy paper (about 0.37), and with no paper block found it falls back to pure white, so the whole sheet becomes ink. Take the paper colour as the dominant smooth background mode of the picture, whatever its saturation, then count blocks as paper when they are close to that colour in chromaticity. Never fall back to white when one smooth colour covers most of the picture. Add tests with kraft (188,148,102) and canary (250,236,158) photos.

Remove what surrounds the sheet before reading the ink. A desk visible on all four sides forms a frame, which dropEdgeMarks keeps on purpose because it does not fill its box. Flood-fill from the picture border over smooth regions whose colour is far from the paper, or find the sheet's quadrilateral, and drop that whole region.

Work out the ink after the person's crop, and filter by the ink the person picks. Today prepare() runs findInk on the uncropped picture, and onlyInk keeps marks of found.hue, not look.ink. So a brown desk makes the box say 'Only the red marks' for a blue stamp and deletes the stamp, and cropping cannot fix it. Recompute found (and the paper map if needed) on the cropped area. Make 'only ink' follow the chosen ink's hue.

Use an edge-preserving background estimate for shadows. With blocks up to 64 px blended bilinearly, a sharp shadow edge in a full-frame photo leaves a dark diagonal streak and fades the ink under the shadow. A per-channel morphological closing (max then min filter, wider than the thickest stroke), or a median background at stroke scale, follows hard shadow edges.

Denoise before thresholding. Apply a small median or bilateral filter to the photo or to the distance plane at photo resolution, and drop islands smaller than a few pixels. Then high-ISO sensor noise does not turn into speckle along every stroke edge, which reads as a photo and not as rubber texture.

Handle faint, dim stamps. Classify ink colour by the hue of the strongest marks, or by chroma relative to how dark each mark is: the 0.22 saturation cut calls faint violet 'black'. Normalise a faint stamp more firmly (the 1.5x cap leaves a grey ghost), up to about 2.5x on the 96th percentile.

Correct a slanted view. Offer four-corner perspective or a 'make it round' step that fits an ellipse to the outer ring of a round seal and unstretches it, or at least a one-axis squash control. A 12 percent keystone already prints the seal as an obvious oval.

Clean up after printed text crossing the ink. Where a dark non-ink mark cuts through a stroke and both sides are ink, fill the gap at the neighbouring ink strength. Remove small disconnected fragments of the old text near the stamp.

Make the photo test samples honest. In samples 4 and 5 the shadow and the table never touch the stamp, and the paper is near-neutral. Add samples with a shadow edge through the stamp, kraft and yellow paper, the whole sheet on a brown desk, high-ISO noise and keystone, and render them like the existing renders.

Outside the photo lens, the impressions are still too even. Strengthen density variation (a darker rim on strokes, a visible heavier side, voids in solid areas such as the logo disc), and use a duller, slightly darker pad-ink tone so solid areas do not read as a flat semi-transparent graphic.

done.item: Texture sized in millimetres at the printed size, not pixels (judges 1 and 2)
done.how: rubber() in src/lib/stampink.ts takes the print size (impression(p, look, maxSide, mm), default 40 mm; Settings passes the stamp's size_mm) and sizes everything in mm: about 40 voids of 0.15 to 0.6 mm on a 40 mm seal, each kept below 0.9 of the stroke it sits in; paper grain at 0.15 and 0.3 mm; mottling about 3.5 mm; two or three ink-starved patches 3 to 8 mm across. Checked at 96 dpi, 200 percent, 150 dpi and 300 dpi.
done.test: stamps.test.ts 'rubber: sized in millimetres...': void count and size in mm, and voids get larger in pixels when the same stamp prints at 20 mm

done.item: Full ink in the cores, unevenness from local variation, opacity raised
done.how: Cores reach alpha 1.0. Mottling and grain only ever lighten, so they are not a fade over everything. STAMP_OPACITY is now 0.97 in src/lib/stamps.ts, used by the CSS and by pdf-lib.
done.test: 97th percentile of core alpha is at least 250; the PDF's ExtGState ca equals STAMP_OPACITY; the CSS regex expects 0.97

done.item: A visible heavier side and a faint arc
done.how: Pressure is even over roughly the heavier third, then drops to about 58 percent on the far side (g = 0.42 at the default). On 60 percent of seeds a short arc of the outer edge fades by 55 to 80 percent. Nothing in a stroke goes below 38 percent except the arc and the voids.
done.test: Heaviest third against lightest third is above 1.25x; 10th percentile of core alpha is at least 85

done.item: Ink squeezed to the edges: darker rims, lighter middles of wide solids
done.how: A distance-to-edge map, in mm. The middle of a wide solid (more than 0.25 mm from the edge) prints up to 16 percent lighter. The rim (within 0.08 to 0.22 mm) carries a rim value that colourise() uses to darken the colour by up to 16 percent.
done.test: The rim of the wide bar prints darker than its middle

done.item: Rough, slightly spread edges instead of a 3x3 blur
done.how: soften() and the baked rotation were removed. Instead the plane is blurred by 0.07 mm and cut again against a noise field (cells of 0.1 and 0.4 mm), with about 0.03 mm of ink spread. The cut is capped at 0.7 of the local peak, so hairlines never break.
done.test: A 0.12 mm hairline and 1 mm type stay intact in the judge faint photo; the thin line stays 1 to 3 px wide

done.item: Duller, darker stamp-pad colours, varied within the impression
done.how: New INK_RGB values print at 0.97 as blue-violet (40,44,128) at hue 238, carmine (170,30,48), violet (80,40,120), blue-black (35,36,48) and a dull green. colourise() mixes toward a lighter, cooler THIN tone where ink is starved or thin, darkens rims, and drifts slightly across the stamp.
done.test: Hue stays within 14 degrees of pad red with more than 3 distinct colours; full ink is dark red; blue and purple hue and darkness bounds

done.item: Logo (sample 6): no deleted wording, orange is not red, no pale tinted disc
done.how: A design (flat paper, isPhoto false) prints solid like rubber: cut steepened to lo+0.1, so a tint becomes full ink. lookFor(seed, ink, prepared) keeps every mark for designs (onlyInk false) and turns on colourGaps for designs with several colours: a 0.22 mm paper gap is cut into the lighter colour wherever two colours meet, so the leaf and its vein stay visible inside the disc. findInk now finds colours peak first (orange at 36 and red at 358 stay separate) and weights fills at 0.12 against lines, so the navy 'GreenCo' decides the ink (blue). The maker has a 'Keep the shapes apart' control and plainly says a logo made for screens looks less like a real stamp than a one-ink design or a photo of the real stamp.
done.test: 'a logo: every mark kept in one ink...': disc, leaf, name and tagline all solid; 1 ink run across the disc without gaps and 3 with them; orange and red told apart

done.item: Ruled lines on lined paper (sample 5): bands and spurs
done.how: ruledLines() looks for 4 or more long, thin, evenly spaced, nearly level lines by voting over angles from -12 to 12 degrees. unrule() then paints each line out with the colour between the pixels just above and below it, so where a line crossed the ring it becomes ring ink. A single long line (a box frame) is never taken for ruling. Only runs on photos.
done.test: Synthetic lined photo: ruled >= 8 and the ring is whole at every angle

done.item: Coloured paper (kraft, canary), a desk round the sheet, hard shadows, noise (judge 3)
done.how: paperOf() takes the paper's own chromaticity as the most common colour of blocks that are not strongly coloured, so kraft and canary count as paper. followShadows() adds a per-channel closing on a 480 px copy, which follows a hard shadow edge. offSheet() floods in from the picture border over smooth non-paper cells, and only when an open sheet is left inside. dropEdgeMarks() also drops thick bands and small scraps (photos only). median3 denoise and despeckle are photo only. New mainMarks() keeps only the stamp, so a stray line from the sheet edge cannot shrink it in its field.
done.test: 'photos: brown kraft and yellow copy paper, a desk...' covers kraft, canary, desk, lined paper, hard shadow, a stray line and heavy noise

done.item: Faint photographed stamps keep their small print (judge 2)
done.how: The cut comes from the picture's own histogram (Otsu, cutOf), with a floor just above the paper grain. In photos it is also set per block of about 1 percent of the picture (strengthOf), so small print under a line of big letters is kept. onlyInk now measures chroma against how dark a pixel is and keeps light, colourless pixels within about 1 mm of kept ink.
done.test: Faint small-print marks stay as ink (at least 5 of 6); the judge photo /tmp/judge-1-1/in-faint-photo.jpg now keeps 'Reg. No. LSK/2019/04417' and 'P.O. BOX 40217-00100 NAIROBI'

done.item: Ink found after the crop; 'Only the X marks' follows the chosen ink
done.how: impression() crops the picture, the paper map and the distance plane first, then runs findInk on what is left and returns it as result.found. onlyInk takes the chosen ink when the picture has marks in it. In photos a coloured colour with a 12 percent share beats black print. The maker's notice and checkbox label use the colour that is actually kept.
done.test: 'photos: faint small print...': with red chosen the red marks are kept, with blue the stamp; cropping recomputes the ink

done.item: Printed text crossing the ink: bites and fragments
done.how: In onlyInk, a dark rejected pixel with kept ink on both sides along a row or column is filled at the neighbours' strength. Despeckle and mainMarks remove small fragments.
done.test: Black print across the ring is gone, the ring is whole where it crossed, and the print inside the ring is gone too

done.item: Slanted view: make it round
done.how: ovalOf() checks whether the outline lies on one ellipse; makeRound() stretches the shorter side. Look.round defaults on for photos, and the maker shows a 'Make it round' checkbox when an oval is found.
done.test: An oval with ratio about 1.22 is found and made square to within 5 percent; a box stamp is no oval; the default is on for photos and off for designs

done.item: Tilt applied by the page, not baked into the pixels (judge 2: RECEIVED 8 to 10 percent too small)
done.how: The picture is now stored straight and the stamp keeps a 'turn'. It is added to lookOf, StampMeta, a new stamps.turn column in COLUMNS, publicStamp, stampSeen and the PUT /sign/:token/stamp answer. The maker, dialog and Settings send turn = tilt. CSS turnStyle rotates the image on the signing page, editor, maker and settings. pdf.ts turns it about the field centre with degrees(page rotation - turn). Old stamps have turn 0, so a tilt drawn into their picture is not applied twice. The API description documents 'turn'.

changes: Express 'short of ink' as lost coverage, not as lower alpha. In rubber() the pad-short patches (patches with smooth(1, 0.35, dd)), the rocking arc (arcDepth * smooth(...)) and the 'inner' solid lightening all multiply v smoothly, which produces soft round blooms with gaussian edges (the 'C' of RECEIVED, the star centres in 7 and 9, the rings in 5, 10 and 12, the logo disc in 6). Instead, turn 'starved' into a threshold against a fine fibre-like noise field (0.05 to 0.2 mm, a little anisotropic). Starved areas then break into speckle and voids with hard-ish edges, while the ink that does land stays near full strength. No light area should have a smooth radial falloff.

Rework the pressure lean (lean = smooth(0.3, 1, ...), g up to 0.42 to 0.6). Today it is a straight tonal ramp across the whole stamp, which reads as a gradient fill (sample 1: navy at top left to periwinkle at bottom right). Keep the tonal difference to about 15 to 20 percent. Put the rest of the effect in the outer few millimetres of the light side as thinner, broken strokes and segments of the outer edge that did not print, with crisp ends, not a fade to white.

Drop or greatly reduce the shift to THIN_RGB in colourise(). Real thin pad ink keeps the same hue and looks lighter because paper shows through the grain. Pastel, periwinkle and lavender washes in the light areas read as a screen tint. Keep one ink colour and vary coverage and density.

Give solids real rubber texture. Large filled shapes (the logo disc, the stars) should print dense with many small salt-like voids (0.1 to 0.3 mm, more of them in solids than in thin strokes) and a slightly darker rim. Today they are a pale even wash, 16 percent lighter in the middle, plus blooms (sample 6 disc median about 119,122,174).

Make the ink-squeeze rim and the edge bleed visible at real print sizes. Today rim darkening is 0.16 times rim over 0.08 to 0.22 mm and edge wander is about 0.06 mm (measured), which is under a pixel at 96 dpi and makes clean designs (samples 1, 2, 3) look vector-perfect on screen. Add a faint 0.05 to 0.1 mm outward bleed at partial alpha, a slightly stronger darker rim, and rarer larger rubber flaws (0.2 to 0.5 mm nicks, 1 to 3 mm waviness on rings), so a perfect circle never survives.

Raise the minimum natural tilt. tiltFor() allows 0.6 degrees (sample 1 got 0.6, which reads as software-aligned). Use a floor of about 1.5 degrees in the -4 to 4 range. Also add a small seeded offset so the stamp does not sit dead-centre on the field and its rule.
For photo sources, drop isolated sub-0.2 mm specks outside the main mark (sample 13's grey dust from removed text). If you keep any splatter, keep only a few larger, ink-coloured dots near the rim.
For the red ink, consider a slightly warmer, duller red (towards vermilion, about 190,45,40) or offer it for name seals. The current carmine (167,23,42) looks pinkish on the square chop in sample 3.

Add renders where the stamp lands on dense body text, not only on a label and a rule. The current 39 images never show it over paragraphs. I checked it myself (/tmp/judge-2-0/sheet-print300-*.png): multiply and 0.97 opacity work and the text stays fully black, so this is about proving it in the test output.

changes: Make ruled-line removal unable to delete ink (src/lib/stampink.ts unrule). Paint out a pixel only where it matches the rule's own profile: its thickness and its lighter, cyan-blue colour. Leave it alone where ink continues above or below it, or where the dark run along the rule is wider than the rule. A stroke lying along a rule, like the E of VALLEY or the inner ring where it runs tangent, must survive. Add a test where a horizontal letter bar and a ring tangent sit exactly on a rule.

When printed text is removed from a photo (onlyInk), fill the stamp ink that was under each crossing from the stroke on both sides of it (inpaint along the stroke direction) rather than leaving a hole. Then despeckle the faint residue left in empty paper areas, such as the blue dust around UMOJA in sample 13. The I of RECEIVED must stay an I.

Never let the unevenness erase words. Cap the faint arc and the pressure fall-off over glyphs: keep text strokes at least about 65 to 70 percent ink, and let the hardly-printed arc fall only on rings and borders. Check this at phone page scale (about 3.4 device px per mm at 390 CSS px, DPR 2), where CITY, UMOJA and MOSHI currently fade out.

Replace the single smooth linear pressure gradient, and the soft-edged faint arc, with irregular, grainy unevenness. Light areas should break up into ragged dry-rubber texture with hard-edged speckle, not soft white glare streaks or smooth fades. The soft white bands on rings (samples 1, 5, 7, 9 to 13) and the band over 'CE' (sample 2) read as reflections on a photo.

Make the rubber visible at print size: edge wander of about 0.05 to 0.15 mm with small bites and slight ink squash, and voids of 0.2 to 0.5 mm with hard edges. Letter and ring outlines should no longer look font-perfect at 200 percent or in the 150 dpi PDF. Today's 0.03 to 0.09 mm wander and pinholes vanish at real size.
Tone down the rim-darker, centre-lighter effect on wide solids, or make it irregular. Stars and discs currently look bevelled or glossy (samples 7, 9, 12).

Logos and designs with tinted fills: threshold design fills to solid ink, as the module comment promises, or let the user choose solid or outline. Never print a translucent mid-tone tint, since a rubber stamp cannot print one (sample 6 disc).

Scale the texture to the printed size and stroke width. For small seals (under about 20 mm) and strokes under about 0.4 mm, reduce the patches, the inner lightening and the fade so complex characters (藤, 澤) keep full-density inner strokes. For red name seals, keep the impression dense and saturated rather than pink and hazy.

Add render checks that read the result, not just the pixels. For each sample, compare the impression against the texture-0 version: no stroke of the design may be fully removed, every glyph keeps its shape, and the hairline rings stay continuous apart from small voids. Run this at 96 dpi, at phone page scale and at 150 dpi.

per_sample.looks_like: The paper colour is gone, but its fibres became ink.

changes: Replace the 'short arc that hardly printed' and the 'patches where the pad ran short' with real ink starvation. Today they multiply alpha by a smooth falloff, which renders as a feathered white glow (glare or airbrush) on almost every stamp (4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 2). Instead, threshold the stroke against fine noise so coverage breaks into grain and speckle, erode the outer edge of the ring inward on the light side so the stroke thins, and never let a smooth translucent wash cross letters. Cap the depth so no part goes paler than a broken-grain look.

Remove the smooth 'inner lighter, rim darker' gradient on wide solids (rubber(): inner and rim, and colourise() dark). It makes stars and the logo disc look domed or bevelled. Use mottled salt-and-pepper coverage inside solids with only a very narrow (about 0.1 mm) darker rim.
Make voids irregular: small clusters of grain-shaped gaps from thresholded noise, not crisp perfectly round white holes.

Handle paper creases and folds, the most common real-world case. Detect long, thin, straight dark and bright line pairs at any angle (not only ruled-paper horizontals) and paint them out along the line before ink detection. Make sure edge and desk removal (offSheet, dropEdgeMarks, mainMarks) can never delete a ring that a crease crosses. Add a folded-letter photo to tests/out/stamp-samples and to tests/stamps.test.ts.

Normalise each pixel by the local paper brightness (paperOf already estimates it) so ink under a glossy highlight or right at a shadow edge is recovered. Stop deciding photo vs design from noise alone: a real phone photo of glossy or clean paper is classified as a design today, which skips onlyInk, median and the round fix. Add a glossy-highlight sample.

When printed text or ruled lines are removed and a stamp stroke continues on both sides of the removed band, rebuild the stamp stroke across the band (inpaint along the stroke). This fixes VALLFY, RECEJVED, the four gaps in sample 5's inner ring and the arrowhead asterisks. Also drop the small ink-coloured fringes that removed black letters leave behind (the specks along the text rows in 13).

In photos, drop marks whose colour does not match the ink: neutral dark specks (paper fibres, dust) and thin isolated flecks not joined to the main strokes. Recycled paper's fibres must not become stamp ink. Add a fibre-flecked grey paper sample.

Close the hairline cut and the pale step a hard shadow edge leaves where it crosses a stroke. Blend the paper estimate across the edge (smaller blocks or an edge-aware filter near strong straight brightness steps), then close 1 to 2 px gaps along strokes.

For photos, skip or compensate the outward ink spread (blur 0.07 mm plus a cut below half), because the photo already holds real spread. Today photo strokes come out visibly bolder than the original and counters close (HARDWARE, UMOJA, APPROVED).

Keep the photo's ink character. Map a dull wine or aubergine ink to a dull red-violet pad ink rather than a clean violet (sample 8), and keep a faint impression somewhat faint, or offer a strength control, instead of always boosting it to full (sample 11).
Correct perspective with a homography fitted to the outer ring, not only an axis stretch, so the top and bottom text match in size after a slanted photo (sample 12).

What already works and should stay: paper removal on kraft, canary, grey, a desk and a hard shadow is clean, with no grey halo on a dark background, no paper texture, no shadow blotch and no tint. Multiply at 0.97 lets the line and words show through. The size is about 40 mm, the tilt is small and the ink colours are dull pad colours.

done.item: 1. Table security_events: account, time, who (user, API key, operator or system), internet address, browser, kind, what it is about, details JSON with no secrets; a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE except the purge after SECURITY_LOG_DAYS (default 400)
done.how: New table at the end of SCHEMA in src/server/db.ts, with seq, outcome and a per-account hash chain (prev_hash/hash) from G12. Two triggers: one refuses every UPDATE. The other refuses a DELETE while the line is younger than the days in the one-row table security_log_keep and its account still exists. purgeSecurityLog() in the cron tick writes SECURITY_LOG_DAYS into that table, deletes older lines and the lines of accounts that are gone. An AFTER DELETE trigger on accounts removes the account's record. Details go through a filter that drops secret-named keys and values that look like keys, signing secrets or password hashes. Who is stored by id only, never an email address. Operator and system lines store no IP and no browser. verifySecurityChain() checks the chain from the oldest line still kept. The chain check, a forged line and the purge are all tested.
done.test: tests/seclog.test.ts: 'a line cannot be changed or deleted, a forged one breaks the chain, old lines go after SECURITY_LOG_DAYS and all go with the account'

done.item: 2. record(kind, ...) in src/server/seclog.ts, called with one line from each place
done.how: Calls are in place for: sign-in succeeded and failed, written to every account of the person; signed out, one browser or everywhere else; password changed and reset; email changed; two-step login on (or moved), off, reset by an admin and reset by email; Google or Microsoft connected (from Settings, by vouched address, or after the code) and removed; member invited, joined (all three ways), removed, role changed and left; owner handed over; API key made and revoked; key first used from a new internet address (router.ts, capped at 50 per key per day); webhook added and removed (host only, because the path often holds a secret); export (everything or selected); envelope taken out of the lists, deleted for good and put back; template rules (values plus a count of chosen members, no names); account settings via PATCH /account (old and new values, the logo by name only) and the 'everyone needs two-step' setting; account closing started and undone; operator pause, resume, trust and untrust. Attacker-minded choice: for a login with two-step on, a wrong password writes nothing at /auth/login, and the code step writes 'wrong_password_or_code' for both cases. Otherwise an admin of a shared team could use the record to tell whether a password was right.
done.test: tests/seclog.test.ts, tests 1 to 8 (each line written once, with the right person, IP and accounts; nothing secret anywhere)
done.left_open: 'webhook changed' is not written because no route can change a webhook. Profile edits (PATCH /me) are not written. Google and Microsoft connect and remove lines exist in the code but have no test (that needs the OIDC fake from signin.test.ts). A two-step sign-in abandoned at the code screen leaves no line. done.item: 1. Account rule (admins, a Settings component of my own): keep closed envelopes for 30 to 9,999 days counted from when they closed, off by default; a template can have its own period
done.how: accounts.retention_days/level/name/code and envelopes.retention_days (templates), added to COLUMNS in db.ts. setPolicy/periodFor/closedAt in src/server/records.ts. GET/PUT /account/retention in src/server/routes-retention.ts. The closing time is completed_at, or else the 'Envelope voided' / 'Declined' / 'Envelope expired' audit line. A field left out of PUT keeps its value. dry_run answers how many closed envelopes the rule would reach at once, and the Settings screen asks before saving those. Admins can add a schedule name and code (G11). The screen is src/components/settings/RetentionSettings.tsx, under Settings, Your data; members see the rule read-only.

done.item: 2. Purge level chosen in the rule: documents; documents and typed values; all that plus personal details replaced by 'Removed on <date>'
done.how: removeDocuments/removeValues/removePersonal and purgeEnvelope in records.ts. Each level also does everything the levels below it do. Words for each level are LEVEL_REMOVES in src/lib/retention.ts. documents: pages (a file a template or another envelope still uses is kept), signed PDF (its SHA-256 is kept in envelopes.purged_sha256), copies made before a correction, signer attachments, stamp pictures, and attachments on our stored email copies. Blobs are taken off the disk. values: field values, signature and initials pictures, comment text, decline and void reasons. personal: names, emails, phones, IPs and browsers on recipients, group members, earlier signatures, comments, disputes, texts, signer codes and audit lines; also the message, names in the subject, our email copies and the webhook log. finalretry.ts no longer retries a purged envelope.
done.test: 'each level removes exactly what it says' (files off the disk, a template's shared file kept, every level checked)
done.left_open: Stamp-picture removal is in the code but has no test of its own. At the personal level, names inside free text are replaced by matching the known strings. A string the software never stored as a name (for example a nickname typed into a comment) is not caught.

done.item: 3. Queue: one email to the sender and the admins 14 days before; Keep it with a reason in the audit trail; admin Hold on an envelope or a folder (reason and setter recorded, lifted only by an admin); the timer purges what is due
done.how: retentionTick in records.ts runs from cron.ts. It sends each person one email with their list and sets retention_queue.noticed_at. Nothing goes until at least 14 days after that email. Switching the rule off, or making the period longer, calls off what was announced and writes an audit line. A level raised after the email does not apply to that email's envelopes. POST /envelopes/:id/keep keeps the envelope for one more period and writes the reason to the audit trail. Holds use legal_holds and legal_hold_items. isHeld(ids) in records.ts is checked by DELETE /envelopes/:id (for-good path), Purge now, the timer, purgeEnvelope itself, POST /me/delete (refused, listing the holds) and purgeUser/purgeClosedAccounts (G11). A folder hold covers what is in the folder, what is added later, and what is moved out (PATCH folder calls holdsFollow). Placing a hold cancels any pending purge. Every refused attempt is recorded. Members see that an envelope is held, not why. API keys with the 'send' scope cannot place or lift holds. Operator override (critic): POST /operator/holds/:id/lift needs two different operators within 7 days; both go on the record and the admins are emailed. An open dispute also blocks a purge.
done.test: 'the 14-day email goes once...', 'a level raised after the email...', 'Keep it...', 'legal hold: every way of deleting...', 'legal hold: closing the account...', 'the people who run the server lift a hold only as two...'
done.left_open: Holds can be placed on one envelope or one folder only. G11 also asked for holds by search, person or date range; not built. The email uses ds-retention's 14 days, not G11's 30. The timer queries each closed envelope of every account that has the rule on, on every tick, and one email lists everything due. Very large accounts were not measured.

done.item: 4. Purge one envelope now: sender or admin picks the level on a closed envelope; it waits 14 days, can be cancelled, then cannot be undone
done.how: POST /envelopes/:id/purge {level} emails the sender and the admins at once. DELETE /envelopes/:id/purge cancels it (409 with code 'rule' when the purge comes from the rule, not a request). Drafts and envelopes still out are refused. A second request at the same moment is refused by a single conditional UPDATE. At the personal level, the name of the person who asked stays out of the envelope's record and is kept in the retention record. The envelope page has a Purge now dialog that shows each level and what stays.
done.test: 'Purge now: closed only, 14 days, called off in that time, then for good'

done.item: 5. A redacted audit trail keeps its chain values and marks each changed line; the page says 'Some details were removed on <date>. The record can no longer be recomputed for those lines.' instead of 'Record was altered'
done.how: audit.redacted_at is set on every line a purge changes. verifyChain in envelopes.ts (small edit) checks a redacted line only for its place in the chain, and only when redacted_at equals the envelope's purged_at; it returns redacted and redacted_on. The envelope page shows redactedNote from lib/retention.ts and a 'Details removed' badge on each changed line. Any other change still shows as altered, including a redaction mark on an envelope that was never purged.
done.test: 'after a purge: /verify says ... the trail says redacted, not altered' (including the two tamper cases)
done.left_open: Someone with write access to the database could mark extra lines of a purged envelope as redacted. The chain never protected against database writers (CHAIN_TRUTH already says so).

done.item: 1. src/server/convert.ts recognises a file by its bytes, never its name: OOXML, OpenDocument, old Office (D0 CF 11 E0), RTF, HTML, plain text (valid UTF-8, no NUL), TIFF; refuse a zip past 100 MB or 20 times its packed size
done.how: detect() in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/convert.ts reads the ZIP central directory, then really unpacks and counts every entry (streamed, stops at the budget), so a ZIP that lies about its sizes is refused too. It also refuses ZIP64 and packing methods office programs never use. OOXML is told apart by [Content_Types].xml plus word/, xl/ or ppt/. OpenDocument needs 'mimetype' as the first local entry (text, spreadsheet, presentation and their templates). Old Office files are read from the compound file's directory entries (WordDocument, Workbook/Book, PowerPoint Document); EncryptedPackage means a password. RTF starts with {\rtf. HTML is a doctype, <html, or <head/<body near the start. Text must be valid UTF-8 with no NUL; UTF-16 and Latin-1 text get 'save as UTF-8' advice. TIFF is II*/MM*, and its pages are counted. Unknown kinds get a plain sentence each: GIF, WebP, HEIC, BMP, program, XML/SVG, ZIP archive, EPUB, Outlook .msg, Pages/Numbers/Keynote. With no converter set up, nothing is unpacked at all.
done.test: tests/convert.test.ts: 'every kind is recognised from its bytes, and the name does not decide' (a Word file named scan.pdf is converted; a PDF named Contract.docx stays a PDF) and 'a zip bomb is refused before anything opens it, whatever sizes it claims' (honest sizes, sizes that lie, one entry listed 18 times past 100 MB, LZMA packing).

done.item: 2. Two converters chosen by settings: CONVERTER=soffice (fresh profile per job, --convert-to pdf, CONVERT_TIMEOUT_MS kills the process group, CONVERT_MAX_JOBS queue, temp files removed) or CONVERTER_URL Gotenberg; neither means uploads behave as before and the refusal names the types; converter without network, README says how
done.how: Each LibreOffice job runs with detached:true in its own process group, which is killed whole on timeout and again on exit. The runner waits until the group is gone before removing the job folder. Each job gets a fresh -env:UserInstallation profile whose registrymodifications.xcu switches macros off and blocks untrusted referer links, and a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG only, no server secrets). Where `unshare -rn` works, every job runs inside it, so it has no network. The first use checks that and logs loudly when it does not work. CONVERTER_URL (or CONVERTER=gotenberg) posts to /forms/libreoffice/convert with an AbortSignal timeout. The queue hands a free place straight to the next job; one account may run at most 2 jobs at once and 60 an hour; past 10x CONVERT_MAX_JOBS waiting, the answer is a 503. CONVERTER=stub is for tests and ignored when NODE_ENV=production. A LibreOffice that cannot be started means the feature is absent: GET /me converts=false and the 'needs a converter' refusal. README 'Turning office files into PDF' explains how to block the network: unshare -rn, a wrapper on PATH, a user with outbound traffic dropped, or Gotenberg on a docker network created with --internal.
done.test: 'a job that runs too long is killed with everything it started, and its folder goes': a stand-in soffice that hangs with a background child. Both are dead, no sg-convert-* folder is left, its environment has no FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, APP_SECRET, DATA_DIR or STRIPE values, and /proc/net/dev shows only lo. The same test covers a LibreOffice that makes no PDF and one that is missing. 'at most CONVERT_MAX_JOBS run at once...': start,end,start,end with MAX_JOBS=1, and a third upload from one account is refused 429. 'one account converts at most 60 files an hour'. 'with no converter, uploads behave as before...'. 'the real LibreOffice turns a Word file, a sheet, a web page and a text into PDFs': real soffice 24.2.7.2 under unshare; the text read back from the PDFs includes Grüße, café and Größe, and an HTML page pointing at a remote picture converts without waiting.

Macro switch-off and link blocking rely on LibreOffice's own settings; no real macro document was tried.

repair:pay-round4.notes_for_owner:
Changes in what the code and API do:
(1) Billing emails no longer leave inside the account's queue. They are written as 'queued' rows and sent after the step. So the answer to Cancel and other billing steps comes before the email does. The plan history line for a reminder is written once its email has gone. The price-notice route waits at most 20 s for its emails and returns two new lists, on_the_way and too_late.
(2) POST /billing/pay-open answers 409 with code 'cancel_pressed' when a Cancel was pressed and the provider never confirmed it. Only {keep: true} pays and keeps the plan. The Plan page asks first. Person-only route, so nothing changed in openapi.
(3) Pressing Cancel again within a day of the plan ending now answers 200 with the same reference and why 'already_ended', instead of 400.
(4) The rule for what counts as ours is now stricter. Being a customer of ours is no longer enough: an invoice must carry our price, our sg_account mark, or a subscription of ours. One from our customer that names none of these is not counted, not refunded and not mailed, and the operators get an alert. Before, it was counted, or refunded as "already cancelled". billing5 now expects this.
(5) Our refunds no longer go to a charge found by amount. When the charge cannot be found by id, a refund the customer asked for answers 502, nothing changes, and a person is told.
(6) A small refund the software sends by itself for an overcharge no longer stops a payment from lifting the new-account limits (STANDING_PAYMENT). README, .env.example and the openapi intro say so.
(7) New columns: payments.tax_cents, refunds.hand_parts, recipients.person_gens.
(8) "You can finish now" emails to form visitors follow the complaint, pause, closing, switched-off and fake-notice rules. The 503 text promises an email only to someone we may email.

Promises in the copy I added or changed:
- The single "Refund sent" email lists each hand part and its day.
- The 'manual' email and the Plan page say how much is back and what is left.
- The closing email names a refund that is with a person, and says we cannot email about it once the account is gone.
- The limits sentence on the Plan page.
- The operator page's "still on the way" and "not told in time" sentences.
- The pay-open question.

Needs a decision:
(a) RENAME: free self-signing under a renamed profile is still a known limit. A monthly cap is one option.
(b) Whether a visitor who started a form before it was switched off may still finish and use a signature. Today they can.

Things to delete by hand: none. The dev data folder /tmp/tmp.8Ixkd5GedY and .next-pay-round4 are already removed.

done.item: Skeptic 1 / bug: a month's signatures carried over by parking them on placeholder envelopes
done.how: A held signature is now for the person and the documents that were sent. In credits.ts, when another person is put on a request the old hold is let go and the new person is held from that moment, in a lot that can still pay today; reholdEnvelope does the same when the documents of an envelope that is out are replaced. Where there is nothing of today's to hold, the change is refused before anything is saved (swapRefusal / pastDateText), through all four doors: quick correct (new address, and another name at the same address), the full editor (PUT), and the signer's 'pass it on' (403 in words that say nothing of the sender's business, and 'you can still sign it yourself'). Small guards added in src/server/envelopes.ts (changeRecipient x2, reassignRecipient, correctEnvelope). Extending the deadline for the same person and the same documents still keeps the hold: that is the brief's rule 5.

done.how: Already built and kept: seal.ts, sealpdf.ts (incremental update, 32 KB Contents, ByteRange), sealcms.ts (content-type, message-digest, signing-certificate-v2, no signing-time, time in /M), der.ts, x509.ts. No new dependency; pkijs/asn1js from the government brief not used. RSA keys sign with RSASSA-PSS, P-256 with ECDSA.

done.how: Already built and kept in tsa.ts: TSA_URL or TSA_URLS (comma list, tried in order), TSA_USER/TSA_PASSWORD, TSA_TRUST; the answer is checked (status, imprint, nonce, time-stamping purpose, validity, trust when set). done.left_open: Honest difference from the government brief: no retry through the finalretry timer. When no service answers, the file is sealed at B-B at once and never upgraded later. The last person's Finish can wait up to 20 seconds when every time-stamp service hangs (said in the README); the designer's note says 'never a signer wait', so the integrator may want a shorter limit. Without TSA_TRUST the issuer of the time stamp's certificate is not checked (documented).

new_bugs.title: /verify says 'its digital seal holds, not a byte has changed' for a forged file that shows different pages
new_bugs.where: src/server/seal.ts findSeals and checkSeal; shown by src/app/verify/SealResult.tsx
new_bugs.detail: The seal is located by a regular expression over the raw bytes (last '/ByteRange [...]' wins, the true one is skipped when bytes[r1] is not '<'), and the gap is read with every non-hex character thrown away. Remove the real Contents value, re-insert '<cms hex>' plus any objects plus a fake '<< /SubFilter /ETSI.CAdES.detached /ByteRange [0 x y z] >' anywhere later: the covered bytes are again the original P+S, so the digest and signature verify. Result intact:true, whole_file:true, ours:true. poppler shows the attacker's page ('FORGED: pay 1,000,000 to Mallory') and pdfsig finds no signature, while our public page vouches for the file with the operator's name. The red 'No match' is above it, but the seal paragraph directly contradicts it. Reproduce: node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test tests/out/verify-ds-seal/probe.test.ts (test A); files forged-shows.pdf, forged-gap.pdf, screenshot verify-forged-phone.png. A smaller variant (attacker bytes inside the real gap, same length) also gives whole_file:true while pdfsig says the field is not signed.

done.item: HIGH: /verify said 'its digital seal holds, not a byte has changed' for a forged file (seal moved, other pages in the gap; bytes hidden in the real gap)
done.how: src/server/seal.ts findSeals and checkSeal rewritten. A seal is reported as holding only when: the /ByteRange text is in the same object as the /Contents it leaves out and lies in covered bytes; '/Contents' stands directly before the gap; the gap is strictly '<' + hex digits + '>' (no whitespace, nothing filtered away); only zeros follow the CMS DER; exactly one signer; digest and signature verify; and, for a seal claiming the whole file, pdf-lib reading the file finds a signature field whose /V has that very ByteRange. A ByteRange that does not line up is now reported as a seal that does NOT hold (was: skipped or null). checkSeal and sealForVerify are now async (one 'await' added in routes-account.ts). SealResult.tsx wording: 'nothing in it has changed' and, when it does not hold, 'or put together around a seal taken from another file ... Do not rely on this file.' new_bugs.title: An uploaded HTML file can pull a picture from the server's own disk into the PDF
new_bugs.where: src/server/convert.ts bySoffice() (HTML handed to LibreOffice unchanged; unshare -rn removes the network but not the file system) and the 'external' check in detect()
new_bugs.detail: , and are loaded by LibreOffice's HTML import despite BlockUntrustedRefererLinks, and the picture is embedded in the PDF the uploader then downloads. Proven through POST /files on a real server and in tests/out/verify-ds-convert/probe-img.ts (EMBEDDED for three variants; , table/td backgrounds, ODT/DOCX/RTF links were all blocked). Any signed-in account can read any image file the server user can read if it knows or guesses the path; on a machine where unshare does not work the same route is a way to make the server fetch URLs. No note is raised (notes=[]), so the screen and the README say nothing was fetched. Fix: sanitise HTML before converting (drop background attributes and non-data: url()/src/href), or run the job in a mount namespace or bwrap sandbox that sees only the job folder; add a regression test with a local PNG.

new_bugs.title: A 1 KB spreadsheet makes the converter use more than 1.4 GB of memory before the timeout
new_bugs.where: src/server/convert.ts runGroup()/bySoffice(): no memory limit on the job
new_bugs.detail: An ODS with one row repeated 1,000,000 times and one cell repeated 1,000 times has nothing to unpack, so the zip check passes. LibreOffice reached 1,488 MB RSS within the 25 s I allowed and was still growing; the default timeout is 60 s, CONVERT_MAX_JOBS is 2 by default, and one account may run 2 at once and 60 an hour. The job is killed and cleaned up correctly, but a small server can be pushed out of memory first. README says 'a few hundred MB per job'. Fix: prlimit --as / ulimit -v or a cgroup limit on the job, a test with this file, and a true number in the README (tests/out/verify-ds-convert/probe-macro.ts).

done.item: HIGH: an uploaded HTML file could pull a picture from the server's disk into the PDF
done.how: Two independent walls. (1) src/server/convert-html.ts: a web page is never handed to the converter as uploaded. Every address is taken out first (background, src, href, srcset, url(...), @import, link, base, frames, objects, meta refresh, on* handlers, any unlisted attribute whose value reads like an address or path, also when spelled with entities, CSS escapes, comments, no quotes, or an unclosed tag; charset declarations like UTF-7 are dropped). Only data: pictures inside the page and clickable http/https/mailto links stay. Anything removed raises the 'external' note. The kept original is the page as uploaded. (2) src/server/convert-box.ts: where `unshare -rnmpf` works, LibreOffice runs with no network, its own process list and a file system of its own (pivot_root, old root unmounted) holding only LibreOffice, system fonts and the job folder as /work; the app folder and DATA_DIR are masked even if under /usr. Fallbacks: no-network only, then nothing; the server log says which. Skeptic's probe-img.ts re-run: all 16 attack cases 'no', the data: control still embeds. External detection now also catches bare paths in ODT and RTF INCLUDEPICTURE.
done.test: tests/convert.test.ts: 'a web page is converted without anything it names outside itself, however it is spelled' (22 spellings), 'the box a job runs in holds LibreOffice and the job folder, and nothing else of this machine', 'the real LibreOffice: a page cannot pull a picture from the disk into the PDF, boxed or not...' (run once with the box and once with no wall at all), 'a text file with no words is refused, and other files that name outside content are noted'
done.left_open: For Word, OpenDocument, RTF and the like there is no cleaning of ours: on a machine where the box cannot be built they rely on LibreOffice's own BlockUntrustedRefererLinks (held in every probe). README says so. The box test runs here as real root; not tried as an unprivileged user or inside the hardened Docker image (where unshare is not permitted, so it falls to level 3 as before). No per-job process-count limit (a fork bomb needs code execution in LibreOffice first).
