checks.item: 1. Signers know before they sign (line by Finish, line in the email, nothing to approvers, viewers, copies)
checks.evidence: tests/impact.test.ts passes 14 of 14. My probes (tests/out/verify-impact/probe.test.ts): a trial signature and the sender's own signature get finish 0 and no email line; an approver gets {finish:0,done:null} before and after, and its real finished screen in a browser has no tree word (approver-done-phone.png); a reassigned signer and both members of a group get the email line and are truly paid; the second signer in a signing order gets finish 0 until their turn, then 10. Screens looked at: finishline-small.png (320x568, own row above Finish, no sideways scroll), finishline-phone.png, finishline-desktop.png (light text in the toolbar, 200 px, beside Finish). No tree words on the consent screen at 320. Emails about a document end with 'Sent with GrowSigning.' only, no money words.
checks.still_broken: The line appears only once Finish is the button, so someone who got the link without the email (text message, link passed on by the sender) learns it at the very end, not 'near the top of the first screen' as the brief asked. This follows the designer's note. The email for an in-person signing goes to the host and tells the host '10 mangroves will be planted with Treegens when you finish.'
checks.suggested_fix: Leave as the designer decided, or have the owner confirm that the end-only line is enough. Reword the host's email line to name the person signing.

checks.item: 2. The first time: signer
checks.evidence: Real Finish tap in a browser with paid answers at 320, 390 and 1280: card appears under the Done card in about 0.9 s, picture runs 2.48 s, one iteration (done-phone-top.png mid-animation, signer-first-paid-phone-end.png, signer-first-paid-desktop.png). Real free first signature shows the logo leaf and 'You signed your first GrowSigning', no planting words (signer-real-free-phone.png). Shown once (server 'seen').
checks.still_broken: See new bugs: walk-in signers under the host's address, and a free first signature followed by a paid one.
checks.suggested_fix: See new bugs.

checks.item: 2. The first time: sender (first envelope of an account)
checks.evidence: sender-first-free-phone.png and sender-first-free-small.png: on a phone the card sits 1,157 px down the envelope page (1,438 px at 320 wide), under the status card, the waiting card and the edit bar. SenderTrees starts the picture at mount (Mangroves go defaults to true) and posts 'seen' at mount, unlike SignerDone which waits until it is on screen. So on a phone the animation plays off screen and is marked as shown; a sender who scrolls later finds a still picture, and it never plays again. On a desktop 1440x900 it starts at y 617, only partly in view (sender-first-free-desktop.png).
checks.still_broken: The sender's first-send animation is not seen on a phone and is used up without being seen.
checks.suggested_fix: Give SenderTrees the same IntersectionObserver start and 'seen' timing as SignerDone, or place the card directly under the 'Sent' card.

checks.item: 3. Later times: small line and running count
checks.evidence: Works for the plain case (test: second paid signature, first false, total 20, '10 more mangroves'). Fails in three probed cases: (a) probe C2: two walk-in signers hosted under the host's address; the second, a different person, reads '10 more mangroves. You have planted 20 mangroves by signing on GrowSigning.' (b) probe B: free first signature then a paid one reads '10 more mangroves' although none were planted before. (c) probe J: counts are only written when someone opens the finished screen or the signing record is built with the box on; with the switch off and nobody opening the finished screen, 2 paid finished signatures give 0 rows, account trees 0, and the signer's later total says 10 instead of 20.
checks.still_broken: Counts credited to the wrong person in person; 'more' said when nothing came before; counts missing from the ledger of paid signatures.
checks.suggested_fix: Key in-person signers by recipient, not by the host's address. Say '10 more' only when total is above this signature's trees. Call noteSigned from the code path that completes a recipient (one line in completeRecipient) instead of lazily.

checks.item: 4. Never in the way (no block, Close, Escape, tap, focus, screen reader sentence, reduced motion, no flashing, 320 and desktop, shown once)
checks.evidence: Browser measurements: Download PDF answers 200 while the picture runs and is above the card at all three sizes; Close is 44 px or more; Tab order on the finished screen is Skip, View, Download, Close, Report, Help with no trap; Escape and Enter on Close remove the card and focus moves to the small card; live region holds one heading, picture is aria-hidden; with reduced motion 0 running animations and a still end picture (signer-first-reduced-phone.png); animations are opacity and transform once, 2.48 s, nothing repeats; no sideways scroll at 320, 390, 1440; after reload it is not shown again.
checks.still_broken: Not tried with a real screen reader. After Close the focus lands on a card with outline none, so a keyboard user sees no focus mark until the next Tab. At 320x568 the signer card is wholly below the fold (y 569) and plays only when scrolled to. The title says 'You just planted 10 mangroves' while the line under it says '10 mangroves are being planted'.
checks.suggested_fix: Give .imp-small:focus-visible a focus ring. Pick one tense for title and line.

checks.item: 5. The server decides every claim

checks.item: 7. Green claims review

checks.suggested_fix: A person checks Treegens' public pages and the three references before launch; add a source for the CO2e factor or drop the figure; publish something checkable for the money (receipts or a Treegens statement of totals received and the rate).

new_bugs.title: Template 'Send now' with a required detail ends in a loop
new_bugs.where: Templates page, Use dialog (the refusal comes from the send check in src/server/customfields.ts, EDITOR_HOW); screenshot tests/out/ux-ds-custom-fields/template-send-now-refused-390.png
new_bugs.detail: An account with one required detail and a template without a value for it: Use, Send now is refused. The dialog never showed the box, the message points to 'the last step of the editor' and names the API field, and the filled button is 'Try sending again', which fails the same way every time. A draft copy is left in Documents. Fix: show required details that the template does not fill as boxes in the Use dialog; for this refusal replace 'Try sending again' with 'Fill in Case number' that opens step 3 with the box focused. Words: 'This template has no Case number, and your account asks for one on every document. Type it here, then send.'

new_bugs.title: A refused send names the API on the sender's screen and leaves the person to find the box
new_bugs.where: Editor step 3 (src/server/customfields.ts EDITOR_HOW; src/components/editor/CustomFieldsStep.tsx); screenshots editor-step3-send-refused.png and editor-step3-send-refused-full.png
new_bugs.detail: Pressing Send with a required detail empty shows: 'Not sent yet. Your account asks for "Case number" on every envelope, and it has no value here. Fill it in on the last step of the editor, under Details (in the API: "custom_fields"), then send again.' The person is already on the last step; '(in the API: "custom_fields")' is a technical name on the daily path (P6); focus is not moved, and the box is a full screen further down. Fix: for the screens say 'Not sent yet. Fill in Case number under Details below, then send again.', scroll to the box and focus it. Keep the API wording for API callers only.

new_bugs.title: A yellow notice shows on step 3 before the sender has done anything
new_bugs.where: src/components/editor/CustomFieldsStep.tsx, the 'missing' notice; screenshot editor-step3-send-refused-full.png
new_bugs.detail: 'Fill in Case number before sending: your account requires it.' is shown from the moment the step opens, next to a box already labelled '(required)'. new_bugs.title: Too many words in the Details card on step 3
new_bugs.where: src/locales/en.json customfields.step.intro, customfields.step.printed, customfields.step.not_printed; screenshot editor-step3-desktop.png

new_bugs.title: 'More options' on the Documents list loses keyboard focus and cannot be closed
new_bugs.where: src/components/sender/CustomFieldFilter.tsx line 33 (the button is replaced by the group); screenshots list-closed-desktop.png, list-open-desktop.png
new_bugs.detail: Enter on 'More options' removes the button from the page, so focus falls to the body (measured: document.activeElement is body); a screen reader hears nothing. After opening there is no way to fold it again. The button has aria-expanded=false but no aria-controls, no data-more="screen" and no data-feature, so the script reports it as an unmarked expander once details exist. Fix: keep the button in place as a real toggle (aria-expanded true or false, aria-controls on the group), move focus to the 'Detail' select on open, and add data-more="screen" and data-feature="ds-custom-fields". When the page gets its own More options, move the group inside it, as the builder noted.

new_bugs.title: Filtering by part of a value finds nothing and does not say why
new_bugs.where: src/components/sender/CustomFieldFilter.tsx (hint is class sn-vh, 1x1 px) and the empty state in src/app/app/envelopes/page.tsx line 211; screenshot list-filter-partial-empty.png
new_bugs.detail: Case number '2026' finds 0 envelopes although '2026/114' and '2026/115' exist: the filter matches the whole value only. The only explanation is hidden from sighted people, the placeholder says 'Value, or empty for any', and the empty state says 'No envelope fits this tab and search.' A busy person concludes the documents are gone. Fix, best first: match the start of the value. Otherwise show the hint: placeholder 'The whole value, like 2026/114', and when a detail filter is on, empty state 'No document has exactly this Case number. Type the whole value, or clear the box to see every document that has one.'

new_bugs.title: 'Change them on the last step of the editor' opens step 1, and step 3 then has two different Save buttons
new_bugs.where: src/components/sender/CustomDetails.tsx (link), src/components/editor/CustomFieldsStep.tsx (Save details); screenshots correct-landing.png, correct-step3-changed.png
new_bugs.detail: From the envelope page of a document that is out, the link lands on step 1 'Add'; two presses of Next and a scroll reach Details. There, changing a value leaves the page's main 'Save changes' greyed out with 'No changes yet' and 'You have not changed anything yet', while a separate 'Save details' inside the card is the one that saves. I did not test what happens to a changed detail when the person also changes something else and presses 'Save changes'. Fix: let the link open step 3 scrolled to Details (or edit in place on the envelope page with one Save), and make the page's own 'Save changes' save the details too so the card needs no button of its own.

new_bugs.title: A new person who presses Send before confirming is sent to a banner that is not on their screen
new_bugs.where: src/components/AppShell.tsx (the full-screen editor branch draws no ConfirmBanner); src/server/envelopes.ts line 1226
new_bugs.detail: Sign up on a phone, press Send in the bottom bar straight away: the editor opens with no confirm banner and no mention of confirming (tests/out/verify-simplify-start/20-phone-editor-unconfirmed.png, banner count 0). The send is then refused with 'Type the 6-digit code from our email in the banner at the top of the app', but the editor has no banner. The person has to guess to press Save and close, find the banner on Home, confirm, and come back. I confirmed the missing banner on screen and the refusal through the API (probe F); I did not walk the editor to step 3 to see how the refusal is displayed. This is the first-send flow for anyone who does not type the code first.

new_bugs.title: Deleting an unconfirmed login and signing up again resets the 10-guess cap
new_bugs.where: src/server/confirmcode.ts (verify_code_wrong lives on the users row); POST /me/delete with now:true; POST /auth/signup
new_bugs.detail: Probe C: a login with all 10 guesses used was deleted at once with its password, then the same address signed up again from another IP and got confirm_by_code true with 0 wrong guesses. Each round costs one sign-up (10 per hour per IP) and sends the mailbox owner one email, and gives a 1 in 100,000 chance. The comment in src/lib/confirm.ts promises '10 wrong codes in all'; that holds per login, not per address. A count per address that outlives the login would close it.

new_bugs.title: The right code typed as the 6th try in a minute gets a generic refusal
new_bugs.where: src/server/confirmcode.ts, rateLimit('confirm-code:<id>', 5, 60000) runs before the code is checked
new_bugs.detail: Probe G: after 5 wrong codes the correct code answers 429 'Too many attempts. Please wait a bit and try again.' It worked a minute later. Because six digits submit by themselves, a person fixing typos reaches this quickly, and the message does not say how long to wait or that the code is still good.

new_bugs.detail: Probe H: the code typed in Arabic-Indic or full-width digits answers code_format. It costs no guess, but a person on such a keyboard is told to type the 6 digits they just typed.

done.item: 3. Photo processing finished
done.how: The photo steps left by the previous engineer were sound on all samples. One real bug fixed in onlyInk(): where printed text crossed a stroke, the stroke was only drawn through when it was narrower than the print (a width cap equal to the print's reach), so a normal ring stayed cut. The stroke may now be up to 3.5 percent of the picture wide, and print far from any ink is skipped so the step is not slower. The 'faint small print' failure was the test, not the code: it assumed a fixed 5 pixel margin, and the impression now sits a little off centre by its seed.

new_bugs.title: A design with a tight margin is printed with a flat cut edge through its ring or frame
new_bugs.where: src/lib/stampink.ts impression(): the seeded offset on cropPlane after inkBox(), then rubber()
new_bugs.detail: inkBox() clamps its 2.5 percent margin to the picture, so a design whose ink is 10 px from the border (samples 2, 17, 18, 19, and any stamp a person cropped tightly) has about 1 percent. The crop is then moved by up to 1.4 percent of the side by the seed and the texture spreads ink outward. Result: ink on the last row or column of the stored PNG, a ruler-straight slice through the outer frame. Sample 2: 18 of 24 seeds (seed 1 has 725 of 1000 bottom-row pixels inked), sample 19: 12 of 24, sample 18: 10 of 24, sample 17: 7 of 24, samples 1 and 3: 0. It is in the stored picture, so screen and PDF both show it. Proof: tests/out/verify-stamp/tex.ts and m-clipped.png. 'A different look' picks another seed, but a person does not know that is the cure.

done.item: 2. scripts/backup.mjs, scripts/restore.mjs, round-trip test
done.how: Both scripts existed. Fixed three real faults: (a) on Node 24 the backup failed outright ('options.rate must be a positive integer'), found by running it inside the container, now a large positive rate; (b) the copied database stayed in write-ahead mode, so anything that read it left a -shm file in the backup, now switched to journal_mode=DELETE before it is hashed; (c) the restore's check opened the restored database with the server's code and changed it, so it no longer matched the manifest: the check now works on a copy in '<target>.checking' that is removed afterwards. The test's setup also never sent its envelopes (signing answered 404), which was why all 16 tests failed at the checkpoint.

checks.item: 1. Table security_events with who, address, browser, kind, about, details without secrets; trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE except the purge after SECURITY_LOG_DAYS (default 400)
checks.evidence: Table and triggers are in src/server/db.ts lines 493-507. My probe (tests/out/verify-ds-sec-log/probe2.test.ts) confirmed plain UPDATE and DELETE are refused, and that the delete trigger uses SQLite's own clock, so a skewed app clock cannot purge early (probe P9: purge threw). securityLogDays() accepts 1 to 3650, else 400. But INSERT OR REPLACE with an existing seq rewrote a line past both triggers (actor_id became 'usr_forged').
checks.still_broken: A line can be rewritten with INSERT OR REPLACE: SQLite does not fire delete triggers for REPLACE unless recursive_triggers is on. The chain check caught the first forgery, but the hash is plain sha256 with no key, so I re-chained all lines the same way and verifySecurityChain() and GET /account/security both said the chain was whole. Deleting the newest lines (after UPDATE security_log_keep SET days=0) removed 3 lines and the chain still read as whole, because nothing outside the table holds the head. All of this needs code or database access, not an API call; no route does it.
checks.suggested_fix: Add a BEFORE INSERT trigger that refuses a seq that already exists (or set PRAGMA recursive_triggers=ON so REPLACE fires the delete trigger), and add triggers refusing UPDATE on security_log_keep to anything but the purge's value. Either key the hash (HMAC with a server secret) or stop describing the chain as showing tampering by someone with database access. Tail deletion needs the head sent somewhere else (the daily chain-head export the builder left out).

checks.item: 2. record() called from each place in the brief's list
checks.evidence: Call sites exist for every item in the brief's list except 'webhook changed' (no such route exists; builder disclosed it). tests/seclog.test.ts passes 13 of 13. My probe P6 showed failed sign-ins write one line each and the typed wrong passwords are not stored.
checks.still_broken: Not proven or missing: (a) Google/Microsoft connect, remove and provider sign-in lines have no test (builder disclosed), so I could not prove them. (b) Probe P3: revoking an invitation (DELETE /account/invites/:id, including an admin invitation) writes nothing; asking for a password reset link writes nothing; a request with a wrong API key writes nothing; PATCH /me (name) writes nothing; regenerating recovery codes and forgetting remembered devices have no record call. (c) Signing up creates a session with no signin.succeeded line (only member.joined when it came from an invitation). (d) Other admin-level changes outside PATCH /account are covered only where their owners added calls (archive addresses, custom fields, retention, trees); billing and plan changes write nothing.
checks.suggested_fix: Add a line for an invitation withdrawn, recovery codes regenerated and remembered devices forgotten (all change who can get in). Add the OIDC fake to seclog tests for the three provider lines. Say in README which of the rest are deliberately not written.

checks.item: 3. Settings, Security: admins only, newest first, filter by kind, person and dates, CSV download
checks.evidence: Looked at tests/out/verify-ds-sec-log/desktop.png (1280), phone390.png, phone320.png and member390.png. The record card sits under 'Your sign-in' on the Security tab, newest first, with What happened / Who / From / Until, Show and Download as CSV. No horizontal scroll at 320, no target under 44 px. A member sees the Security tab with only their own sign-in cards and no record; member calls to all four routes get 403 (builder's test, passes). The brief's sentence is shown word for word.
checks.still_broken: Against the designer's note: Alerts and 'Send it to your security system' are two always-open cards, not under the record card's More options; there is no search box (four filters instead); the word 'events' is on the screen twice and 'security.event', 'next_after' and 'webhook' are shown outside any destination form. Kind names and group labels come from src/lib/seclog.ts, not through t(). The builder's keyboard check only shows Tab moving through INPUTs; I did not prove the full keyboard path either.
checks.suggested_fix: Fold the alerts and the security-system section into a closed More options inside the record card, as the designer's note says.

checks.item: 4. GET /api/account/security-events?after=&limit= (up to 1,000) for admins and admin keys, in order with a cursor; opt-in webhook security.event
checks.evidence: Probe P8: after=-1, 1e3, abc and limit=0, 1001, 1.5 each get 400 in plain words; a cursor past the end answers 200 with the same cursor and no lines. Probe P1: a second account's admin sees none of the first account's lines through the API, the view or the CSV, also when filtering by the other person's id. Builder's tests show a member and a send key get 403, an admin key pages in order, and security.event goes only to a webhook that lists it. Documented in src/server/openapi-seclog.ts (6 mentions). Webhook delivery reuses deliver() in webhooks.ts, which resolves the name once, refuses private addresses, pins the connection to the checked addresses and does not follow redirects; a URL with credentials in it was refused (probe P7).
checks.still_broken: With 'names and email addresses' on, a person who was removed from the team is still shown with their name and email address as they are now (probe P4: the API returned the ex-member's new address). The screen always shows an ex-member's current name.

checks.item: 5. Five alerts, on by default, each emails the admins at most once an hour per rule, an admin can switch each off
checks.evidence: Probe P6: 40 wrong passwords from 40 addresses gave 10 refusals, 30 rate-limited, 10 lines and exactly 1 alert email. Probe P5: two API keys in one hour gave 1 alert. Throttle is one atomic upsert in security_alerts_sent. PATCH /account/security is refused to an admin key (builder's test). The email says nobody watches the record.
checks.still_broken: The 'an alert was switched off' email to the other admins is not throttled: 15 off/on toggles sent the other admin 15 emails and wrote 30 lines (probe P5). And because the throttle is per rule, a second, hostile admin-scope key made within an hour of an ordinary one produces no email (probe P5: only key 'one' was announced).
checks.suggested_fix: Throttle the switched-off email (for example once an hour per account) and name every key made in the hour in the next alert, or exempt admin-scope keys from the hourly throttle.

checks.item: 6. Account export and account deletion include the record
checks.evidence: securityExport() yields security/security-events.csv; the accounts_security_gone trigger deletes the lines with the account. Covered by builder's tests 5 and 10, which pass. I did not write a separate probe for this point.

checks.item: Attack: a secret, token, code, password or key in the log or its export
checks.evidence: Probe P7: the raw API key, the webhook signing secret and the session cookie are not in any line; a key pasted as a key's name is replaced by '[left out]'; wrong passwords typed at sign-in are not stored.
checks.still_broken: The secret filter covers details only. The browser name (User-Agent) is stored and exported as sent: a sign-in with User-Agent 'curl Bearer tsk_live_abcdefghijklmnop whsec_zzz' was stored whole. Setting values are stored as typed (an account name of 'Pass: correct horse battery' was kept). The screen and README say the record 'never holds a password, code, key'.
checks.suggested_fix: Run the same value filter over ua before storing it.

checks.item: Attack: one account reading another's log; members and everyday keys reading it
checks.evidence: Probe P1 (cross-account, with person filter and CSV) found nothing foreign. Every query in routes-seclog.ts is bound to c.account.id. Member and send-key 403s are in the builder's passing test.

checks.item: Attack: webhook export to private addresses or through redirects
checks.evidence: POST /webhooks calls assertPublicUrl; deliver() calls resolvePublic at every delivery and connects only to the addresses it checked (src/server/webhooks.ts lines 39-75), with node http.request, which follows no redirect. Read in code; the private-address refusal itself is tested in the existing webhook tests, not by me.

checks.item: Attack: the log growing without bound
checks.evidence: Failed sign-ins are capped by the login limit (10 per address of a login per 15 minutes; probe P6 wrote 10 lines for 40 tries). New-address lines are capped at 50 per key per day. CSV refuses over 100,000 lines. Lines go after SECURITY_LOG_DAYS.
checks.still_broken: api_key_addresses is never purged (grep finds no DELETE; rows go only with the key). GET /account/security runs verifySecurityChain() over every line of the account on each open of the screen, and the export builds the whole CSV in memory; neither has a cap. An admin can write unlimited settings.changed lines in their own account by toggling.

checks.item: Attack: the time source
checks.evidence: Lines are stamped by the server's now(); nothing from the client sets a time. The delete trigger compares against SQLite's own clock, so moving the app clock 401 days ahead could not purge anything (probe P9).

checks.item: Docs: README, .env.example, openapi
checks.evidence: README lines 998-1020 (what is in it), 310 (bad reviews table), 1173 (what is not in it), 1357 (configuration); .env.example line 205; openapi-seclog.ts. No em dashes and no old product name in the feature's files.

checks.item: Suite, type check and flow counts
checks.evidence: tests/seclog.test.ts 13 of 13. npx tsc --noEmit clean. npm test: 1318 tests, 1299 pass, 18 fail; the ones I opened (lifecycle 428, platform 396, signin 843 and 1140) fail on date wording and copy from other work, none in seclog. tests/ux/flows.cjs ran every flow; first send 18 actions and 8 screens, signing 7 and 5, all at their ceilings.

Settings now shows 9 tabs where the baseline had 8; I could not attribute the extra choice to this feature rather than the Sending or Stamps tabs.
